data.name: Malaysia
data.summary: Malaysia taxes individuals on Malaysian-source income at up to 30%. There is no capital gains tax for individuals on shares (the 2024 capital gains tax applies to companies and other entities), and foreign-sourced income received in Malaysia by resident individuals is exempt until 31 December 2036 (subject to conditions). Malaysian dividends are exempt except for a 2% tax on annual dividend income above MYR 100,000 from YA 2025. There is no inheritance, estate, gift or wealth tax. Real property gains tax applies to Malaysian property: non-citizens pay 10% even after 5 years. Malaysia has no comprehensive tax treaty with the US, so US dividends bear 30% US withholding.

regimes.name: Malaysian tax resident
regimes.description: Territorial-style taxation: Malaysian-source income at 0-30%; foreign income received by resident individuals exempt to 2036.
regimes.eligibility: Resident if physically present 182 days or more in a calendar year (with linking rules). Non-citizens typically use the MM2H programme.

capital_gains.summary: No general capital gains tax for individuals. Gains on Malaysian real property and shares in real property companies are subject to real property gains tax (RPGT): 30% within 3 years, then 20%/15% (citizens and PRs) or 30% (non-citizens) in years 4-5, and from year 6: 0% for citizens/PRs, 10% for non-citizens. Foreign gains received by resident individuals are covered by the foreign-sourced income exemption to 2036.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Shares (listed or unlisted, Malaysian or foreign) held by individuals: no CGT. RPGT nil for citizens/PR after 5 years.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: The capital gains tax introduced from 1 January 2024 on disposals of unlisted shares and foreign capital assets applies to companies, LLPs, trusts and co-operatives, not individuals (PwC: no general capital gains tax for individuals). A family holding company would be subject to it.

sources.title: Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia - home (RPGT and CGT links)

capital_gains.rate_basis: Individuals: no CGT on shares. Local real estate: RPGT 10% for a non-citizen selling after year 5 (citizens/PR 0%). Foreign real estate: gain is foreign-sourced, exempt to 2036. Headline 30% = top RPGT rate for disposals within 3 years.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Share or property dealing as a business is taxed as business income at up to 30%.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: RPGT rates fall with holding period (6th year onward lowest).
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Foreign income (including gains) received in Malaysia by resident individuals exempt 1 January 2022 to 31 December 2036, subject to conditions; foreign income through a Malaysian partnership is excluded.

dividends.summary: Malaysian single-tier dividends are exempt, but from YA 2025 resident individuals pay 2% on annual dividend income above MYR 100,000 (after eligible deductions). Foreign dividends received by resident individuals are exempt under the foreign-sourced income exemption to 31 December 2036 (subject to conditions), so source-country withholding is the final cost.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: First MYR 100,000 of dividends a year not subject to the 2% tax.
dividends.important_exceptions: No comprehensive treaty with the US (only air/sea transport), so US dividends bear 30% US WHT. Without a treaty, Malaysian credit relief is limited to half the foreign tax (relevant only if foreign income were taxable).

sources.title: Malaysia - Individual - Foreign tax relief and tax treaties

dividends.rate_basis: Domestic: 2% on dividend income above MYR 100,000. Foreign: exempt (FSI exemption for individuals to 2036).
dividends.withholding_outbound: No WHT on single-tier dividends (general rule; not separately verified).
dividends.treaty_network: About 74 comprehensive treaties (PwC lists 78 entries including pending and limited agreements); the US agreement covers only air and sea transport.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Companies pay 24%; since 2024 companies pay CGT on unlisted Malaysian shares and on foreign capital gains received (10% of net gain or 2% of gross for pre-2024 assets, general knowledge, not verified). Foreign dividends received by companies are exempt only with economic substance.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: State quit rent and local assessment rates on property; stamp duty on property transfers (rates not verified). Foreign buyers face state-set minimum purchase prices.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance, estate or gift tax (estate duty abolished in 1991). Transfers of Malaysian real property between parents and children are generally exempt from RPGT, and stamp duty relief applies to some family transfers (not verified).
inheritance.important_exceptions: Reintroduction of an inheritance tax has been discussed publicly but no law exists (general knowledge).
inheritance.gift_tax: None. Stamp duty can apply to transfers of Malaysian property or shares by gift (rates not verified).

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if present in Malaysia 182 days or more in a calendar year (further linking rules for shorter periods exist; not detailed by PwC).

corporate.summary: 24% CIT (SME rates 15%/17% on the first MYR 600,000). Single-tier system. Since 1 January 2024 companies, LLPs, trusts and co-operatives pay capital gains tax on unlisted Malaysian shares and foreign capital assets (details not verified). Pillar Two: QDMTT and MTT from financial years starting 1 January 2025; UTPR not adopted.

income.name: Malaysia

income_tax.summary: Residents pay progressive tax from 0% to 30% (30% above MYR 2 million) after a MYR 9,000 personal relief. Foreign-sourced income received in Malaysia is exempt for residents under an exemption order running to 31 December 2036 (PwC), but not for pay for work done in Malaysia. Foreign employees pay 2% EPF; the self-employed have no mandatory scheme in the sources.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Non-Malaysian employees: EPF 2% with no wage limit; SOCSO employee share capped at MYR 29.75 a month (employment injury and invalidity, small). Non-citizens are outside EIS. Self-employed contributions were not covered on the PwC page; set to 0 and flagged.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income tax. Rebates for chargeable income below MYR 35,000 are not modelled. Bracket start values are lower bounds of each band (rate applies to income above).

sources.title: Malaysia - Individual - Taxes on personal income

open_questions: Self-employed social security (SESKSO/EPF voluntary) not verified.
PwC labels rates 'prevailing' and does not state YA2026 explicitly; reliefs page shows YA2026.

Non-Employment Injury Scheme (0.75% of salary up to MYR 6,000 ceiling, from 1 June 2026) is listed by PwC without saying who bears it or whether non-citizens are in scope; not included in the employee rate.

EPF relief is capped at MYR 4,000 a year (SOCSO relief MYR 350 separately; SOCSO not in the recorded rate): the deductible share is about 0.81 at EUR 54k income (2% = MYR 4,936) and about 0.33 at EUR 134k (MYR 12,249); the field holds one share, 0.81 used.

regimes.name: DE Rantau Nomad Pass
regimes.description: MDEC-run Professional Visit Pass for remote workers and freelancers with foreign employers or clients. Minimum income USD 24,000 a year for tech talent and USD 60,000 for non-tech professionals; 3-12 months with one 12-month renewal (24 months total). The pass itself does not change tax.
regimes.duration_note: USD 24,000 applies to tech roles (non-tech USD 60,000). Pass valid 3-12 months, renewable once for 12 months. Employer or clients must not be registered in Malaysia; passport validity over 14 months at application. A tourist pass cannot be converted.
open_questions: Fees not confirmed (Section C of the FAQ was not read in full).
Whether a pass holder staying 182+ days becomes tax resident and gets the foreign income exemption: see the foreign-income regime.

regimes.name: Foreign-sourced income exemption for resident individuals
regimes.description: Resident individuals are exempt on foreign-sourced income received in Malaysia (all classes except income received from a partnership business in Malaysia), subject to conditions that PwC does not list. PwC gives the period as income received from 1 January 2022 to 31 December 2036. It does not cover a remote worker's pay for work done in Malaysia: PwC's income-determination page says an employee is taxed on employment income earned for work performed in Malaysia regardless of where payment is made, so such pay is Malaysian-sourced, not foreign-sourced. The same sourcing logic applies to freelance services performed in Malaysia. Applies to anyone tax resident, not only pass holders.
regimes.duration_note: Exemption period runs to 31 December 2036 per PwC (about 10 years from 2026). Earlier statements of 2026 or 2030 in other sources are superseded; the gazetted order itself was not opened.
open_questions: Gazetted Exemption Order (PU(A)) and LHDN conditions not opened; end date taken from PwC only.
Whether pay for services performed in Malaysia for a foreign client is Malaysian-sourced under s.3 ITA was inferred from PwC's employment-income sourcing statement, not from LHDN guidance.
